correctness.rationale: Each plant-loss event over subset S has probability q^{|N(S)|}. Its first and second factorial loss moments are sums over singletons and plant pairs; the third factorial moment depends on plant-triple neighborhood unions, and equal lower moments make centered third-moment difference exactly 6 times the triple-union polynomial difference. For fixed (v,k) with k pollinators of 3 plants, weakly ordered multisets of the C(v,3) possible columns enumerate all bipartite graphs up to pollinator relabeling, including identical-neighborhood twins. Inspected source exhaustive verifier and an independently developed enumeration both covered every connected case v+k<=10: connected candidate totals 1,1,7,32,162,1083,7588 (total 8,874), all matching 1-/2-plant signatures having matching triple histograms. On 6 plants/5 pollinators, verified the witness G=(123,145,246,356,123), H=(124,135,236,456,123), identical labeled pair-signatures and distinct triple histograms G {3:1,4:3,5:16}, H {4:5,5:15}. Their centered third moments differ by 6q³(1−q)²>0 for all 0<q<1; the finite cutoff is exhaustively certified rather than extrapolated.
residual_risks: Each of k pollinators has exactly three distinct plant neighbors; twin pollinators allowed; connected bipartite graph and no isolated species.

originality.rationale: The Pasch four-block trade is classical, as are secondary coextinctions in bipartite networks. The new finding is the fixed-q labelled first-two-order indistinguishability versus third centered moment separation with the sharp 11-vertex cutoff under degree-three pollinators and twin neighborhoods. Inspected ecological studies optimize or average different removal statistics, not the exact moment-polynomial and complete minimality. An exhaustive scientific literature survey is not claimed.
residual_risks: Classical combinatorial design literature may contain a stronger minimal nonisomorphic block-trade classification, potentially implying the core 11-vertex bound after interpretation.
The original 2004 coextinction article was not read in full; its exact combinatorial scope remains a historical-priority risk.

value.rationale: Determining the smallest ecological incidence system on which all pairwise coextinction statistics conceal a genuine higher-order risk difference is a motivated finite extremal question. The exact 11-species cutoff, fully specified connected witness and strictly positive all-q skewness separation make a natural, self-contained invariant rather than an arbitrary unmotivated census.
residual_risks: Requires exactly three plant partners per pollinator, twins allowed; findings should not be transferred to other eco-epidemiological removal models without proof.
